questions.q: Why write the success criteria before building the model?
options: SageMaker refuses to start training without them
So you can pick criteria the model already satisfies
They are required by the model registry
So 'done' is testable and you cannot move the goalposts after seeing results
questions.explain: Criteria written first make the project testable. The specific thresholds in this capstone are the author's choices, not AWS requirements.

questions.q: With 38% churn, a model that always predicts 'no churn' has 0.619 test accuracy. What else is true of it?
options: AUC of 0.5 and recall of 0, so it finds no churners at all
It has an AUC of 1.0
It cannot be registered
Its recall is 0.619
questions.explain: The naive baseline is right most of the time but never identifies a churner, which is why accuracy is a poor headline metric here.

questions.q: The first model's recall on weekly plans was 0.162 while monthly plans reached 0.740. What is the best conclusion?
options: The overall recall of 0.556 is enough to report
Report and investigate the weak segment; overall metrics can hide it
Delete the weekly plan customers from the data
The model is perfect on weekly plans
questions.explain: Segment metrics reveal weak spots. Here weekly churn is rare (about 18%), so a 0.5 threshold rarely fires. Record it and revisit it.

questions.q: Why does the capstone keep scaling and encoding inside the scikit-learn Pipeline?
options: Pipelines train faster than plain estimators
SageMaker only accepts Pipeline objects
A deployed model can accept raw columns and training and serving transformations cannot drift apart
It removes the need for a test set
questions.explain: When the whole pipeline is the model, one artifact carries the preprocessing, so serving applies exactly what training used.

questions.q: What is the one rule to follow if you point the capstone code at a real AWS account?
options: Never use scikit-learn
Use the largest instance available
Register every version as Approved
Delete the endpoint when finished, because it bills while it exists
questions.explain: A real-time endpoint keeps instances running until deleted, so cleanup is part of the project.
